subject: art-design
title: Islamic & Mexican Art
welcome_lead: Geometric tiles and bright Day of the Dead skulls.
meta_desc: KS3 cultural art: Islamic geometry and Mexican folk art.
final_note: Pattern and pattern-breaking colours from two cultures.

concepts.def: Geometric tile design from Muslim world.
Decorated skull made for Day of Dead.
Art made by ordinary people, often craft.

walkthroughs.body_html: Islamic art uses geometric patterns — stars, hexagons and tessellating shapes — often in tiles. Religious art avoids images of people, so pattern fills the space.
Day of the Dead (Dia de los Muertos) is a Mexican festival on 1-2 November. Families paint sugar skulls, build altars and remember loved ones with bright colour.
Both traditions are forms of folk art — made by communities, passing skills down. They prove fine art does not only live in galleries.
